finding_dispositions.evidence: Fresh r6 verifier rebuild/replay and targeted tests passed for no-follow initialization, fanout, and post-initialization objects/staging/locks/resources replacement. Descriptor-bound operations reject replaced attested ancestors before external mutation.

The fresh r6 clock regression passed: expiry observation persists repository-owned high-water state, and subsequent clock rollback cannot revive an expired lease. Authoritative time decisions remain transactionally bound to persisted high-water state.

Fresh canonical resource-order and opposing-process tests passed. Cross-token acquisition validates the global canonical sequence before mutation, and opposing two-process requests terminate without deadlock.

The fresh exact claim/reconciliation regression passed. Direct CommitBatch validation binds the complete ordered lease-resource set, fence tokens, task lease, and same-transaction event payload, including missing, extra, empty, stale, and wrong-lease rejection.

Fresh connection tests passed for doctor and backup read-only enforcement. Read-only URI, query_only, and deny-by-default authorizer reject direct writes and WITH-prefixed UPDATE, DELETE, and INSERT statements.

Fresh replay and recovery corruption tests passed. Event indexes, transaction revisions, transaction heads, and task/head state are validated against authoritative replay and fail closed on corruption.

Independent r6 fresh-object probes at object.after_staging_directory_fsync and object.after_publication raised ObjectIntegrityError, cleared wrong staging/final names, left no available metadata, and retained no tampered bytes. Fresh post-commit replacement persisted quarantined metadata and cleared the wrong final.

Independent stateful dedup probes first established an available object, then replaced final during a second same-content put at object.after_object_directory_fsync and object.before_metadata_commit. In both cases the current transaction rolled back, put_verified failed, final and staging were cleared, and a separate transaction durably changed the preexisting metadata to quarantined. The gate-bound regression, normal dedup-success test, fresh replacement test, and 13-step-by-3-kind fault matrix all passed.

The cleanup path records only cleanup_final=true and later unconditionally calls object_directory.unlink(filename), without binding cleanup to the invalid inode. A deterministic scheduler probe delayed only that final unlink after writer A detected a mismatch. During the delay, writer B used a normal ObjectRepository with the same lock registry to successfully put the same digest, verify the final, and commit state='available'. Releasing A then deleted B's newly installed final. This reproduced at both object.after_object_directory_fsync and object.before_metadata_commit; final state was available metadata with a missing canonical file.

findings.summary: Stale pathname cleanup can delete a concurrently installed verified object after the concurrent writer has committed available metadata.
findings.evidence: For each pre-transaction and transaction-window mismatch, writer A published a final that a separate thread replaced, detected the binding failure, and reached final cleanup. An in-memory scheduler barrier delayed only A's BoundDirectory.unlink call. While A was paused, writer B invoked the unmodified public put_verified path using the same repository and lock registry; B returned success, its final contained the approved bytes, and SQLite recorded state='available'. When A resumed, its unconditional unlink(filename) removed B's different, newly verified inode. Both runs ended with writer B successful, metadata available, staging empty, and the canonical final absent. Shared object locks permit the interleaving, and cleanup performs no inode ownership check or writer serialization.
findings.required_fix: Make publication cleanup mutually exclusive with same-digest installation across threads and processes, for example through an attested per-digest publication lock or an equivalent atomic ownership protocol. Cleanup must remove only the invalid inode owned by the failed attempt and must not unlink a different concurrently installed inode; metadata/file visibility must remain coherent. Add gate-bound deterministic two-writer regressions at object.after_object_directory_fsync and object.before_metadata_commit that pause stale cleanup, let a second writer complete, then prove the second final remains readable and available after the first writer exits. Retain the stateful dedup quarantine, fresh/post-commit, normal dedup, and 13-by-3 fault regressions.
